overview.description: Manifests are JSON-encoded configurations that define IBM Cloud services, access policies, service authorizations, and identity provider settings for IBM Technology Zone environments. This guide covers creating manifests for all supported platforms.

supported_platforms.platform: OCPV Multi-VM - Define multiple VM specifications
VPC Multi-VM - Define multiple VMs in IBM Cloud VPC infrastructure
watsonx SaaS Shared - Configure watsonx services
Account Vending - Provision IBM Cloud accounts with services

overview.critical_principle: A single incorrect value will cause the entire Terraform provisioning to fail. Always verify service names, plan names, and JSON structure.

platform.name: OCPV Multi-VM
platform.description: Multi-VM manifests define specifications for multiple virtual machines in an OpenShift Virtualization environment. Each VM can have individual configurations for CPU, memory, storage, networking, and post-deploy customization.

vm_definition_structure.description: Each VM in the manifest is defined with the following structure
vm_definition_structure.structure: { "name": "Required: Unique name for the VM (used in hostname and identification)", "template": "Required: VM template name (certified golden templates: 'itz-rhel9-workstation', 'itz-rhel9-server', 'itz-windows11-ent', 'itz-windows2022-std', 'itz-windows2025-std')", "cpu": "Required: Number of CPU cores (integer)", "memory": "Required: Memory in GB (integer)", "rootDiskSize": "Optional: Root disk size in GB (integer, defaults to global root_disk_size)", "secondaryDiskSize": "Optional: Secondary disk size in GB (integer, defaults to global secondary_disk_size)", "ports": "Optional: Array of port mappings (e.g., ['22/tcp', '80/tcp', '3389/tcp'])", "cloudInit": "Optional: Array of predefined cloud-init module names (e.g., ['rhel-subscription', 'uptycs'])", "customCloudInit": "Optional: Array of custom cloud-init commands to execute", "postDeploy": { "mode": "Optional: Post-deploy mode ('cloud-init', 'ssh', 'container', or 'none'). Defaults to global post_deploy_mode", "repository": "Optional: Git repository URL containing post-deploy code. Defaults to global post_deploy_repository", "branch": "Optional: Branch to checkout. Defaults to global post_deploy_branch", "script": "Optional: Script filename to execute. Defaults to global post_deploy_script", "variables": "Optional: JSON-encoded map of variables. Defaults to global post_deploy_variables", "requirements": "Optional: Ansible requirements file. Defaults to global post_deploy_requirements", "play": "Optional: Ansible playbook filename. Defaults to global post_deploy_play", "ignoreErrors": "Optional: Whether to ignore errors (boolean). Defaults to global post_deploy_ignore_errors" } }

field.name: secondaryDiskSize
field.description: Secondary disk size in GB, overrides global setting
field.default: Uses global secondary_disk_size if not specified

field.name: ports
field.description: Array of port mappings for network access

platform.name: VPC Multi-VM
platform.description: VPC Multi-VM manifests define specifications for multiple virtual machines in IBM Cloud VPC infrastructure. Supports both shared VPC (using existing infrastructure) and create mode (provisioning new VPC). Each VM can have individual configurations for compute profiles, storage, networking, DNS, and post-deploy customization.

manifest_structure.description: YAML structure with three main sections: version, vpc, and optional post_deploy
manifest_structure.structure:
version: "1.0"
vpc: version: "1.0" infrastructure: mode: shared # or "create" # ... infrastructure config vms: - name: vm-name # ... VM config
post_deploy: # Optional pattern-level orchestration mode: container # ... post-deploy config

critical_policy.description: ALWAYS use shared infrastructure mode by default. The create mode (dedicated/isolated VPC) requires special approval and should NOT be offered as an option to users.
critical_policy.approval_process: If a user specifically requests isolated or dedicated VPC infrastructure: 1. Inform them that create mode requires approval 2. Direct them to contact TechZone support at: https://techzone.ibm.com/support 3. They must submit a support request explaining their use case 4. Only proceed with create mode after receiving approval confirmation

mode.name: shared
mode.description: Uses existing VPC infrastructure (DEFAULT and REQUIRED for all deployments)

use_cases.use_case: All standard deployments - leverages existing infrastructure

vm_definition_structure.description: Each VM in the manifest is defined with the following structure

required_fields.field: Operating system type: rhel, sles, ubuntu, windows, zos

optional_fields.field: Boot volume size in GB (default: 100, range: 100-250)
Whether to attach floating IP (default: true)

os.features: VNC, noVNC, Cockpit, patching, hardening, FQDN

post_deploy_configuration.critical_requirement: UNIQUE REQUIREMENT: GitHub deploy keys MUST be stored in TechZone secrets manager. Unlike other patterns, deploy keys CANNOT be set directly in the manifest or as variables.

step.title: Ask User for Repository Name
step.description: When generating manifests with post-deploy automation, you MUST ask the user for their repository name from the ITZ Content organization (e.g., "my-custom-repo").
step.example_prompt:
To configure post-deploy automation, I need your repository name from the ITZ Content organization. Example: If your repo is git@github.ibm.com:itz-content/my-custom-repo.git, provide: my-custom-repo
Please provide your repository name:

step.title: Construct Repository URL and Secrets Path
Inform User About Deploy Key Storage
step.description: After generating the manifest, inform the user that they need to contact TechZone support to store their deploy key in the secrets manager.

support_contact.description: Users must contact TechZone support to have their deploy key stored in the secrets manager. They should provide their repository name and the deploy key value.

step.example_message:
**Important: Deploy Key Setup Required**
To complete your post-deploy configuration, you need to store your deploy key in TechZone's secrets manager:
1. Contact TechZone support at: https://techzone.ibm.com/support 2. Provide the following details: - Repository name: {repository-name} - Secrets path: techzone/itz/provisioning-secrets/itz-content/{repository-name} - Key name: deploy_key - Your deploy key value (the private SSH key for accessing your repository)
TechZone support will securely store your deploy key in the secrets manager, making it available to your environment during provisioning.

per_vm_post_deploy.description: Runs on individual VMs during or after provisioning
per_vm_post_deploy.modes: cloud-init (during boot), ssh (after VM is reachable)

rule.name: Use "playbook" for Ansible Playbooks
rule.description: When the task executes an Ansible playbook (.yml or .yaml file containing Ansible tasks), use the "playbook" keyword instead of "script".

rule.name: Use "script" for Shell Scripts and PowerShell
rule.description: When the task executes a BASH script (.sh) or PowerShell script (.ps1), use the "script" keyword.

per_vm_post_deploy.structure:
post_deploy: mode: cloud-init # or "ssh" version: "1.0"
config: work_dir: "/root/post_deploy_jobs" cleanup: true
jobs: - name: job-name description: "Job description" repository: "git@github.ibm.com:itz-content/REPO_NAME.git" branch: "main"
secret_groups: - type: keymaster path: "techzone/itz/provisioning-secrets/itz-content/REPO_NAME" keys: ["deploy_key"]
tasks: - name: task-name script: "scripts/setup.sh" # Use "script" for BASH/PowerShell # OR playbook: "playbooks/configure.yml" # Use "playbook" for Ansible variables: key: "value"

example_retrieval.description: Use techzone-request-mcp to fetch example VPC Multi-VM environment definitions. This provides real-world examples of manifest structure, VM configurations, and post-deploy automation patterns.

configuration.name: simple_two_vm
configuration.example:
version: "1.0"
vpc: version: "1.0"
infrastructure: mode: shared vpc_name_prefix: itz-vpc-
subnets: 0: count: 1 enable_public_gateway: true
security_group: public_tcp_ports: [2223, 443, 51124, 5986] public_udp_ports: []
vms: - name: rhel-server image_name: ibm-redhat-9-6-minimal-amd64 os_type: rhel profile_name: bx2-4x16

- name: windows-server image_name: ibm-windows-server-2022-full-standard-amd64 os_type: windows profile_name: bx2-4x16
boot_volume_size: 100 enable_public_ip: true primary_subnet_number: 1

config: enable_postinstall: true enable_fqdn: true enable_secure_winrm: true enable_patching: true enable_hardening: true enable_reboot: true

validation_checklist.check: Manifest version is "1.0"
VPC section has version: "1.0"
Infrastructure mode is either "shared" or "create"
All VMs have required fields: name, image_name, os_type, profile_name
Image names match available IBM Cloud stock images
OS types match the selected images
Compute profiles are valid IBM Cloud profiles
Security group ports include all required access ports
DNS is only enabled for VMs with public IPs
Post-deploy repositories exist and deploy keys are in secrets manager
Secret paths use correct format: techzone/itz/provisioning-secrets/itz-content/{repo-name}
YAML syntax is valid (proper indentation, no tabs)

platform.name: watsonx SaaS Shared
platform.description: Manifests for watsonx SaaS Shared configure watsonx.ai, watsonx.data, and watsonx.governance services in a shared environment.

manifest_structure.description: JSON structure with four main sections: services, access, authorizations, and idp.

section.name: services
section.description: Define IBM Cloud services to provision
section.structure: { "services": [ { "friendly_name": "Human-readable service name", "instance": "Optional static instance name", "prefix": "itz", "suffix": "3-char abbreviation", "service": "programmatic-service-name", "plan": "programmatic-plan-name", "parameters": {}, "resource_group_id": "", "region": "", "lock": "true", "enable": "true", "create": "Optional timeout (e.g., '1h', '6h')", "update": "Optional timeout", "delete": "Optional timeout" } ] }

critical_rules.rule: Use programmatic service names from IBM Cloud Global Catalog
Use programmatic plan names from IBM Cloud Global Catalog
Suffix must be 3 characters or less
Lock should be "true" to prevent accidental deletion
Region should be empty string "" unless exception applies
Parameters should be {} unless service requires specific config
Verify supported roles for each service (they vary)
Use comma-separated strings for multiple roles

policy.name: default_access
policy.all_iam_account_management_services_role: Administrator,Service ID creator,User API key creator,API key reviewer

critical_rules.rule: Format as JSON string with service pairs and roles
Default enable to "false", enable only when needed

section.name: idp
section.description: Configure App ID identity provider settings

service_name_resolution.description: Convert marketing names to programmatic names using IBM Cloud Global Catalog

process.step: Identify marketing name from user input
Query IBM Cloud Global Catalog API: https://globalcatalog.cloud.ibm.com/api/v1
Extract programmatic service name and plan name
Verify available roles for access policies

rule.name: Use Double Quotes
rule.description: All string values must use double quotes, not single quotes

rule.name: Boolean as Strings
rule.description: Boolean values must be strings, not native booleans

rule.name: Empty String for Defaults
rule.description: Use empty string "" for optional fields, not null

rule.name: Empty Object for Parameters
rule.description: Use {} for empty parameters, not null

rule.name: No Trailing Commas
rule.description: JSON does not allow trailing commas

convention.description: Default prefix for IBM Technology Zone
convention.rule: Only change if explicitly specified by requirements

requirement.name: Generate ONLY JSON
requirement.description: Output only the JSON manifest, no additional text or explanations

requirement.name: Maintain Exact Structure
requirement.description: Include all required keys and sections

requirement.name: Verify Service Names
requirement.description: Always validate against IBM Cloud Global Catalog

requirement.name: Include Default Policies
requirement.description: Always include standard default access and resource ownership policies

requirement.name: Format JSON Properly
requirement.description: Use proper indentation and valid JSON syntax

requirement.name: Test JSON Validity
requirement.description: Ensure JSON can be parsed (test with jq or JSON validator)

integration_with_terraform.description: Manifests are processed during account provisioning by Terraform

process.step: User requests environment in IBM Technology Zone
User receives provisioned environment with configured access

integration_with_terraform.critical_note: The provisioning process is atomic - if any service fails to provision due to incorrect configuration, the entire process fails and must be retried.
